examples.title: Cost, selling price and profit
examples.problem: An article costing ₹720 is sold at a profit of 15%. What is the selling price?

examples.title: Mark-up and discount
examples.problem: An article costs ₹500. It is marked 30% above cost and sold at a 10% discount. What is the profit percentage?
steps: Profit = 85 on a cost of 500, which is 17%.

examples.title: Successive discounts
examples.problem: What single discount is equal to successive discounts of 10% and 5%?

examples.title: Overall profit on several deals
examples.problem: A trader buys a sofa for ₹20,000 and a table for ₹5,000. He sells the sofa at a 10% profit and the table at a 20% loss. What is his overall profit percentage?
steps: Sofa SP = 22,000 and table SP = 4,000, so total SP = 26,000.
Total CP = 25,000, so the profit is 1,000.

examples.title: False weights
examples.problem: A dealer claims to sell at cost price but gives 950 g for every kilogram. What is his profit percentage?
steps: Take the cost of 1 kg as 100. The buyer pays 100 and gets goods that cost 95.
